nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Aclidinium Bromide in the Treatment of Moderate-to-severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) (LAS-MD-38)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥3% and greater than placebo): headache (6.6% vs 5.0%), nasopharyngitis (5.5% vs 3.9%), and cough (3.0% vs 2.2%)
target_moa: Long-acting antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) agent that inhibits the M3 receptor on airway smooth muscle leading to bronchodilation

advisory_committee.vote: Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) met Feb 23, 2012; voted substantial evidence of efficacy (14 yes, 0 no), safety adequately assessed (10 yes, 3 no, 1 abstention), and in favor of approval (12 yes, 2 no)

description.text: Updated labeling with ASCENT (LAS-MD-45) safety trial results on MACE and reduction in COPD exacerbations, and simplified the indication statement

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application (sNDA) provides for updates to the labeling for Tudorza Pressair (aclidinium bromide) to incorporate results of Study LAS-MD-45 (ASCENT), a post-marketing required safety study, including information regarding major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and reduction in COPD exacerbations. This supplement also provides data for the effect of aclidinium on the St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) score and labeling updates to comply with the requirements of the Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule (PLLRR). The indication statement was simplified for consistency with current labeling practices.

summary.text: Standard 505(b)(1) NDA for a new molecular entity; reviewed with a Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee meeting and approved first cycle with a required postmarketing cardiovascular safety trial.

citations.quote: Forest Pharmaceuticals submitted this 505(b)(1) new drug application for use of Tudorza Pressair (acldinium bromide inhalation powder) for the long-term maintenance treatment of bronchospasm associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema.
A meeting of the Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) was held on February 23, 2012, to discuss this application.
